key_insight: A quantum-assisted agentic DAI framework can meet hard control deadlines while solving microgrid dispatch optimally by selecting the fastest suitable solver and encoding storage value into the decision process.
engineering_relevance: This approach supports real-time, cost-optimal orchestration of hybrid renewable microgrids with storage and demand response under strict operational timing constraints.
method: BDIx agents formulate each dispatch slot as a QUBO problem.
A coordinator agent chooses among quantum, quantum-inspired, and classical solvers based on learned latency beliefs.
A storage valuation mechanism prices stored energy using discounted future-peak value to add intertemporal signal.
evidence_signal: In a 24-hour grid-connected microgrid simulation, the framework missed zero deadlines, matched the exact optimum every slot, achieved 146.24 EUR daily cost, and improved cost by 4.5 percent versus no storage valuation.
watch_item: The reported quantum advantage relies on statevector-simulated QAOA and should be validated on hardware under realistic noise, scaling, and latency variability.
paper_title: A Quantum-Assisted Agentic Distributed Artificial Intelligence Framework for Deadline-Bounded Orchestration of Hybrid Renewable Microgrids
